title: Ocugen Enters Exclusive OCU400 License Agreement With Celairis
summary: Ocugen granted Celairis exclusive rights to commercialize gene therapy OCU400 in Australia, New Zealand and ASEAN, with payments of up to $7.1 million.
body_markdown:
Celairis, a Sydney-based in-licensing, development and commercialization biopharmaceutical company, will be responsible for regional regulatory submissions, market access and commercialization of OCU400. The two companies expect to enter into a supply agreement under which Ocugen will manufacture and supply OCU400. According to the company, the agreement covers a region with an estimated 725 million people.


"This agreement marks our third strategic regional partnership for OCU400," said Dr. Shankar Musunuri, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Ocugen. Matt Zeller, Chief Executive Officer of Celairis, said Ocugen is "the kind of partner Celairis was built for."


## Why It Matters for OCGN


OCU400 has not been approved or registered and is not available for supply in any market of the territory, the release said. Ocugen is conducting the Phase 3 liMeliGhT clinical trial of OCU400, with topline data expected in the first quarter of 2027, followed by planned global regulatory submissions, including a Biologics License Application in the U.S. and a Marketing Authorization Application in Europe. Regulatory submissions in the territory are expected to follow.
